Name: always-on-top
Label: Always on top
Description: Make scrcpy window always on top (above other windows).

Name: angle
Label: Angle
Description: Rotate the video content by a custom angle, in degrees (clockwise).

Name: audio-bit-rate
Label: Audio bit rate (for example 128K)
Description:
Encode the audio at the given bit rate, expressed in bits/s. Unit suffixes are supported: 'K' (x1000) and 'M' (x1000000).
Default is 128K (128000).

Name: audio-buffer
Label: Audio buffer (ms)
Description:
Configure the audio buffering delay (in milliseconds).
Lower values decrease the latency, but increase the likelihood of buffer underrun (causing audio glitches).
Default is 50.

Name: audio-codec
Label: Audio codec
Description:
Select an audio codec (opus, aac, flac or raw).
Default is opus.

Name: audio-codec-options
Label: Audio codec options
Description:
Set a list of comma-separated key:type=value options for the device audio encoder.
The possible values for 'type' are 'int' (default), 'long', 'float' and 'string'.
The list of possible codec options is available in the Android documentation: <https://d.android.com/reference/android/media/MediaFormat>

Name: audio-dup
Label: Audio dup
Description:
Duplicate audio (capture and keep playing on the device).
This feature is only available with --audio-source=playback.

Name: audio-encoder
Label: Audio encoder
Description:
Use a specific MediaCodec audio encoder (depending on the codec provided by --audio-codec).
The available encoders can be listed by --list-encoders.

Name: audio-source
Label: Audio source
Description:
Select the audio source. Possible values are:
 - "output": forwards the whole audio output, and disables playback on the device.
 - "playback": captures the audio playback (Android apps can opt-out, so the whole output is not necessarily captured).
 - "mic": captures the microphone.
 - "mic-unprocessed": captures the microphone unprocessed (raw) sound.
 - "mic-camcorder": captures the microphone tuned for video recording, with the same orientation as the camera if available.
 - "mic-voice-recognition": captures the microphone tuned for voice recognition.
 - "mic-voice-communication": captures the microphone tuned for voice communications (it will for instance take advantage of echo cancellation or automatic gain control if available).
 - "voice-call": captures voice call.
 - "voice-call-uplink": captures voice call uplink only.
 - "voice-call-downlink": captures voice call downlink only.
 - "voice-performance": captures audio meant to be processed for live performance (karaoke), includes both the microphone and the device playback.
Default is output.

Name: audio-output-buffer
Label: Audio output buffer (ms)
Description:
Configure the size of the SDL audio output buffer (in milliseconds).
Do not change this setting unless you have a good reason.
Default is 10.

Name: video-bit-rate
Label: Video bit rate (for example 8M)
Description:
Encode the video at the given bit rate, expressed in bits/s. Unit suffixes are supported: 'K' (x1000) and 'M' (x1000000).
Default is 8M (8000000).

Name: background-color
Label: Background color
Description:
Set the background color, encoded as hexadecimal color code (#RGB or #RRGGBB).
Default is #222 (dark gray).

Name: camera-ar
Label: Camera ar
Description:
Select the camera size by its aspect ratio (+/- 10%).
Possible values are "sensor" (use the camera sensor aspect ratio), "<num>:<den>" (e.g. "4:3") or "<value>" (e.g. "1.6").

Name: camera-facing
Label: Camera facing
Description:
Select the device camera by its facing direction.
Possible values are "front", "back" and "external".

Name: camera-fps
Label: Camera fps
Description:
Specify the camera capture frame rate.
If not specified, Android's default frame rate (30 fps) is used.

Name: camera-high-speed
Label: Camera high speed
Description:
Enable high-speed camera capture mode.
This mode is restricted to specific resolutions and frame rates, listed by --list-camera-sizes.

Name: camera-id
Label: Camera id
Description:
Specify the device camera id to mirror.
The available camera ids can be listed by:
    scrcpy --list-cameras

Name: camera-size
Label: Camera size
Description: Specify an explicit camera capture size.

Name: camera-torch
Label: Camera torch
Description: Turn on the camera torch when the camera starts.

Name: camera-zoom
Label: Camera zoom
Description: Specify the camera zoom initial value.

Name: capture-orientation
Label: Capture orientation
Description:
Set the capture video orientation.
Possible values are 0, 90, 180, 270, flip0, flip90, flip180 and flip270, possibly prefixed by '@'.
The number represents the clockwise rotation in degrees; the flip" keyword applies a horizontal flip before the rotation.
If a leading '@' is passed (@90) for display capture, then the rotation is locked, and is relative to the natural device orientation.
If '@' is passed alone, then the rotation is locked to the initial device orientation.
Default is 0.

Name: crop
Label: Crop
Description:
Crop the device screen on the server.
The values are expressed in the device natural orientation (typically, portrait for a phone, landscape for a tablet).

Name: select-usb
Label: Select usb
Description:
Use USB device (if there is exactly one, like adb -d).
Also see -e (--select-tcpip).
Reason: Selected by the launcher connection settings.

Name: disable-screensaver
Label: Disable screensaver
Description: Disable screensaver while scrcpy is running.

Name: display-id
Label: Display id
Description:
Specify the device display id to mirror.
The available display ids can be listed by:
    scrcpy --list-displays
Default is 0.

Name: display-ime-policy
Label: Display ime policy
Description:
Set the policy for selecting where the IME should be displayed.
Possible values are "local", "fallback" and "hide".
"local" means that the IME should appear on the local display.
"fallback" means that the IME should appear on a fallback display (the default display).
"hide" means that the IME should be hidden.

Name: display-orientation
Label: Display orientation
Description:
Set the initial display orientation.
Possible values are 0, 90, 180, 270, flip0, flip90, flip180 and flip270. The number represents the clockwise rotation in degrees; the "flip" keyword applies a horizontal flip before the rotation.
Default is 0.

Name: select-tcpip
Label: Select tcpip
Description:
Use TCP/IP device (if there is exactly one, like adb -e).
Also see -d (--select-usb).
Reason: Selected by the launcher connection settings.

Name: fullscreen
Label: Fullscreen
Description: Start in fullscreen.

Name: force-adb-forward
Label: Force adb forward
Description: Do not attempt to use "adb reverse" to connect to the device.

Name: gamepad
Label: Gamepad
Description:
Select how to send gamepad inputs to the device.
Possible values are "disabled", "uhid" and "aoa".
"disabled" does not send gamepad inputs to the device.
"uhid" simulates physical HID gamepads using the Linux UHID kernel module on the device.
"aoa" simulates physical gamepads using the AOAv2 protocol.It may only work over USB.
Also see --keyboard and --mouse.
Reason: AOA input is unavailable in this portable native build. SDK and UHID availability depends on the device and selected input.

Name: help
Label: Help
Description: Print this help.
Reason: Prints information and exits; this is a diagnostic action, not a saved streaming setting.

Name: keep-active
Label: Keep active
Description: Keep the screen on by simulating user activity.

Name: keyboard
Label: Keyboard
Description:
Select how to send keyboard inputs to the device.
Possible values are "disabled", "sdk", "uhid" and "aoa".
"disabled" does not send keyboard inputs to the device.
"sdk" uses the Android system API to deliver keyboard events to applications.
"uhid" simulates a physical HID keyboard using the Linux UHID kernel module on the device.
"aoa" simulates a physical keyboard using the AOAv2 protocol. It may only work over USB.
For "uhid" and "aoa", the keyboard layout must be configured (once and for all) on the device, via Settings -> System -> Languages and input -> Physical keyboard. This settings page can be started directly using the shortcut MOD+k (except in OTG mode) or by executing: `adb shell am start -a android.settings.HARD_KEYBOARD_SETTINGS`.
This option is only available when a HID keyboard is enabled (or a physical keyboard is connected).
Also see --mouse and --gamepad.
Reason: AOA input is unavailable in this portable native build. SDK and UHID availability depends on the device and selected input.

Name: kill-adb-on-close
Label: Kill adb on close
Description: Kill adb when scrcpy terminates.
Reason: ADB is shared with other programs; the launcher manages its lifecycle.

Name: legacy-paste
Label: Legacy paste
Description:
Inject computer clipboard text as a sequence of key events on Ctrl+v (like MOD+Shift+v).
This is a workaround for some devices not behaving as expected when setting the device clipboard programmatically.

Name: list-apps
Label: List apps
Description: List Android apps installed on the device.
Reason: Prints information and exits; this is a diagnostic action, not a saved streaming setting.

Name: list-cameras
Label: List cameras
Description: List device cameras.
Reason: Prints information and exits; this is a diagnostic action, not a saved streaming setting.

Name: list-camera-sizes
Label: List camera sizes
Description: List the valid camera capture sizes.
Reason: Prints information and exits; this is a diagnostic action, not a saved streaming setting.

Name: list-displays
Label: List displays
Description: List device displays.
Reason: Prints information and exits; this is a diagnostic action, not a saved streaming setting.

Name: list-encoders
Label: List encoders
Description: List video and audio encoders available on the device.
Reason: Prints information and exits; this is a diagnostic action, not a saved streaming setting.

Name: max-size
Label: Maximum resolution (longest edge, pixels)
Description:
Limit both the width and height of the video.
For display mirroring, the other dimension is computed so that the device aspect ratio is preserved (except for flex displays).
For camera mirroring, the value is used to select the camera source size instead.
Default is 0 (unlimited).

Name: max-fps
Label: Maximum frame rate (FPS)
Description: Limit the frame rate of screen capture (officially supported since Android 10, but may work on earlier versions). This is an upper limit, not a guaranteed frame rate, and does not increase the frame rate of the source video.

Name: min-size-alignment
Label: Min size alignment
Description:
Configure the minimum video size alignment.
This is a power-of-2 value (1, 2, 4, 8 or 16) that the video width and height must be multiples of.
The actual alignment will be the maximum of this value and the video codec's alignment requirement.
Default is 1.

Name: mouse
Label: Mouse
Description:
Select how to send mouse inputs to the device.
Possible values are "disabled", "sdk", "uhid" and "aoa".
"disabled" does not send mouse inputs to the device.
"sdk" uses the Android system API to deliver mouse eventsto applications.
"uhid" simulates a physical HID mouse using the Linux UHID kernel module on the device.
"aoa" simulates a physical mouse using the AOAv2 protocol. It may only work over USB.
In "uhid" and "aoa" modes, the computer mouse is captured to control the device directly (relative mouse mode).
LAlt, LSuper or RSuper toggle the capture mode, to give control of the mouse back to the computer.
Also see --keyboard and --gamepad.
Reason: AOA input is unavailable in this portable native build. SDK and UHID availability depends on the device and selected input.

Name: mouse-bind
Label: Mouse bind
Description:
Configure bindings of secondary clicks.
The argument must be one or two sequences (separated by ':') of exactly 4 characters, one for each secondary click (in order: right click, middle click, 4th click, 5th click).
The first sequence defines the primary bindings, used when a mouse button is pressed alone. The second sequence defines the secondary bindings, used when a mouse button is pressed while the Shift key is held.
If the second sequence of bindings is omitted, then it is the same as the first one.
Each character must be one of the following:
 '+': forward the click to the device
 '-': ignore the click
 'b': trigger shortcut BACK (or turn screen on if off)
 'h': trigger shortcut HOME
 's': trigger shortcut APP_SWITCH
 'n': trigger shortcut "expand notification panel"
Default is 'bhsn:++++' for SDK mouse, and '++++:bhsn' for AOA and UHID.

Name: no-control
Label: No control
Description: Disable device control (mirror the device in read-only).

Name: no-playback
Label: No playback
Description: Disable video and audio playback on the computer (equivalent to --no-video-playback --no-audio-playback).

Name: new-display
Label: New display
Description:
Create a new display with the specified resolution and density. If not provided, they default to the main display dimensions and DPI.
Examples:
    --new-display=1920x1080
    --new-display=1920x1080/420  # force 420 dpi
    --new-display         # main display size and density
    --new-display=/240    # main display size and 240 dpi

Name: no-audio
Label: Disable audio
Description: Disable audio forwarding.

Name: no-audio-playback
Label: No audio playback
Description: Disable audio playback on the computer.

Name: no-cleanup
Label: No cleanup
Description:
By default, scrcpy removes the server binary from the device and restores the device state (show touches, stay awake and power mode) on exit.
This option disables this cleanup.

Name: no-clipboard-autosync
Label: No clipboard autosync
Description:
By default, scrcpy automatically synchronizes the computer clipboard to the device clipboard before injecting Ctrl+v, and the device clipboard to the computer clipboard whenever it changes.
This option disables this automatic synchronization.

Name: no-downsize-on-error
Label: No downsize on error
Description:
By default, on MediaCodec error, scrcpy automatically tries again with a lower definition.
This option disables this behavior.

Name: no-key-repeat
Label: No key repeat
Description: Do not forward repeated key events when a key is held down.

Name: no-mipmaps
Label: No mipmaps
Description: If the renderer is OpenGL 3.0+ or OpenGL ES 2.0+, then mipmaps are automatically generated to improve downscaling quality. This option disables the generation of mipmaps.

Name: no-mouse-hover
Label: No mouse hover
Description: Do not forward mouse hover (mouse motion without any clicks) events.

Name: no-power-on
Label: No power on
Description: Do not power on the device on start.

Name: no-vd-destroy-content
Label: No vd destroy content
Description:
Disable virtual display "destroy content on removal" flag.
With this option, when the virtual display is closed, the running apps are moved to the main display rather than being destroyed.

Name: no-vd-system-decorations
Label: No vd system decorations
Description: Disable virtual display system decorations flag.

Name: no-video
Label: No video
Description: Disable video forwarding.

Name: no-video-playback
Label: No video playback
Description: Disable video playback on the computer.

Name: no-window
Label: No window
Description: Disable scrcpy window. Implies --no-video-playback.

Name: no-window-aspect-ratio-lock
Label: No window aspect ratio lock
Description: Disable window aspect ratio lock.

Name: orientation
Label: Orientation
Description: Same as --display-orientation=value --record-orientation=value.

Name: otg
Label: Otg
Description:
Run in OTG mode: simulate physical keyboard and mouse, as if the computer keyboard and mouse were plugged directly to the device via an OTG cable.
In this mode, adb (USB debugging) is not necessary, and mirroring is disabled.
LAlt, LSuper or RSuper toggle the mouse capture mode, to give control of the mouse back to the computer.
Keyboard and mouse may be disabled separately using--keyboard=disabled and --mouse=disabled.
It may only work over USB.
See --keyboard, --mouse and --gamepad.
Reason: OTG and AOA support are disabled in this portable native build; use SDK or UHID input instead.

Name: port
Label: Port
Description: Set the TCP port (range) used by the client to listen. Default is 27183:27199.

Name: pause-on-exit
Label: Pause on exit
Description:
Configure pause on exit. Possible values are "true" (always pause on exit), "false" (never pause on exit) and "if-error" (pause only if an error occurred).
This is useful to prevent the terminal window from automatically closing, so that error messages can be read.
Default is "false".
Passing the option without argument is equivalent to passing "true".
Reason: The launcher runs without a console. Use the connection window and log files to inspect errors.

Name: power-off-on-close
Label: Power off on close
Description: Turn the device screen off when closing scrcpy.

Name: prefer-text
Label: Prefer text
Description:
Inject alpha characters and space as text events instead of key events.
This avoids issues when combining multiple keys to enter a special character, but breaks the expected behavior of alpha keys in games (typically WASD).

Name: print-fps
Label: Print fps
Description: Start FPS counter, to print framerate logs to the console. It can be started or stopped at any time with MOD+i.

Name: push-target
Label: Push target
Description:
Set the target directory for pushing files to the device by drag & drop. It is passed as is to "adb push".
Default is "/sdcard/Download/".

Name: record
Label: Record
Description:
Record screen to file.
The format is determined by the --record-format option if set, or by the file extension.

Name: raw-key-events
Label: Raw key events
Description: Inject key events for all input keys, and ignore text events.

Name: record-format
Label: Record format
Description: Force recording format (mp4, mkv, m4a, mka, opus, aac, flac or wav).

Name: record-orientation
Label: Record orientation
Description:
Set the record orientation.
Possible values are 0, 90, 180 and 270. The number represents the clockwise rotation in degrees.
Default is 0.

Name: render-driver
Label: Render driver
Description:
Request SDL to use the given render driver (this is just a hint).
Supported names are currently "direct3d", "opengl", "opengles2", "opengles", "metal" and "software".
<https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL_HINT_RENDER_DRIVER>

Name: render-fit
Label: Render fit
Description:
Set the render-fit mode to configure how the rendering fits the window.
Possible values are "letterbox", "stretched" and "unscaled".
"letterbox": preserve the aspect ratio and fit the window as best as possible (black bars are added either at the top and bottom or at the sides if needed).
"stretched": fit the window without preserving the aspect ratio.
"unscaled": render the display without scaling.
Default is "letterbox", unless --flex-display is set, in which case it is "unscaled".

Name: require-audio
Label: Require audio
Description: By default, scrcpy mirrors only the video when audio capture fails on the device. This option makes scrcpy fail if audio is enabled but does not work.

Name: serial
Label: Serial
Description: The device serial number. Mandatory only if several devices are connected to adb.
Reason: Selected by the launcher connection settings.

Name: turn-screen-off
Label: Turn screen off
Description: Turn the device screen off immediately.

Name: screen-off-timeout
Label: Screen off timeout
Description: Set the screen off timeout while scrcpy is running (restore the initial value on exit).

Name: shortcut-mod
Label: Shortcut mod
Description:
Specify the modifiers to use for scrcpy shortcuts.
Possible keys are "lctrl", "rctrl", "lalt", "ralt", "lsuper" and "rsuper".
Several shortcut modifiers can be specified, separated by ','.
For example, to use either LCtrl or LSuper for scrcpy shortcuts, pass "lctrl,lsuper".
Default is "lalt,lsuper" (left-Alt or left-Super).

Name: start-app
Label: Start app
Description:
Start an Android app, by its exact package name.
Add a '?' prefix to select an app whose name starts with the given name, case-insensitive (retrieving app names on the device may take some time):
    scrcpy --start-app=?firefox
Add a '+' prefix to force-stop before starting the app:
    scrcpy --new-display --start-app=+org.mozilla.firefox
Both prefixes can be used, in that order:
    scrcpy --start-app=+?firefox

Name: show-touches
Label: Show touches
Description:
Enable "show touches" on start, restore the initial value on exit.
It only shows physical touches (not clicks from scrcpy).

Name: tcpip
Label: Tcpip
Description:
Configure and connect the device over TCP/IP.
If a destination address is provided, then scrcpy connects to this address before starting. The device must listen on the given TCP port (default is 5555).
If no destination address is provided, then scrcpy attempts to find the IP address of the current device (typically connected over USB), enables TCP/IP mode, then connects to this address before starting.
Prefix the address with a '+' to force a reconnection.
Reason: Selected by the launcher connection settings.

Name: time-limit
Label: Time limit
Description: Set the maximum mirroring time, in seconds.

Name: tunnel-host
Label: Tunnel host
Description:
Set the IP address of the adb tunnel to reach the scrcpy server. This option automatically enables --force-adb-forward.
Default is localhost.

Name: tunnel-port
Label: Tunnel port
Description:
Set the TCP port of the adb tunnel to reach the scrcpy server. This option automatically enables --force-adb-forward.
Default is 0 (not forced): the local port used for establishing the tunnel will be used.

Name: version
Label: Version
Description: Print the version of scrcpy.
Reason: Prints information and exits; this is a diagnostic action, not a saved streaming setting.

Name: verbosity
Label: Verbosity
Description: Set the log level (verbose, debug, info, warn or error). The default depends on whether the native client was built with debug logging.

Name: v4l2-sink
Label: V4l2 sink
Description:
Output to v4l2loopback device.
This feature is only available on Linux.
Reason: Available only on Linux, not in this Windows package.

Name: v4l2-buffer
Label: V4l2 buffer
Description:
Add a buffering delay (in milliseconds) before pushing frames. This increases latency to compensate for jitter.
This option is similar to --video-buffer, but specific to V4L2 sink.
Default is 0 (no buffering).
This option is only available on Linux.
Reason: Available only on Linux, not in this Windows package.

Name: video-buffer
Label: Video buffer (ms)
Description:
Add a buffering delay (in milliseconds) before displaying video frames.
This increases latency to compensate for jitter.
Default is 0 (no buffering).

Name: video-codec
Label: Video codec
Description:
Select a video codec (h264, h265 or av1).
Default is h264.

Name: video-codec-options
Label: Video codec options
Description:
Set a list of comma-separated key:type=value options for the device video encoder.
The possible values for 'type' are 'int' (default), 'long', 'float' and 'string'.
The list of possible codec options is available in the Android documentation: <https://d.android.com/reference/android/media/MediaFormat>

Name: video-encoder
Label: Video encoder
Description:
Use a specific MediaCodec video encoder (depending on the codec provided by --video-codec).
The available encoders can be listed by --list-encoders.

Name: video-source
Label: Video source
Description:
Select the video source (display or camera).
Camera mirroring requires Android 12+.
Default is display.

Name: stay-awake
Label: Stay awake
Description: Keep the device on while scrcpy is running, when the device is plugged in.

Name: window-borderless
Label: Window borderless
Description: Disable window decorations (display borderless window).

Name: window-title
Label: Window title
Description: Set a custom window title.

Name: window-x
Label: Window x
Description:
Set the initial window horizontal position.
Default is "auto".

Name: window-y
Label: Window y
Description:
Set the initial window vertical position.
Default is "auto".

Name: window-width
Label: Window width
Description:
Set the initial window width.
Default is 0 (automatic).

Name: window-height
Label: Window height
Description:
Set the initial window height.
Default is 0 (automatic).

Name: flex-display
Label: Flex display
Description: Continuously resize the virtual display to match the window.
